Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 How to Play 3 Potions 4 Characters Overview You are an adventurer descending into a deadly dungeon. Work solo or with an ally to reach the final room on the fourth floor and defeat Og's Remains to retrieve Og's Blood. How to Play Room cards will be shuffled and laid out in a 3 x 3 grid. Choose a character card (see Characters for details), then start in the upper left Room. Move left to right, top to bottom, to reach the bottom right card and move to the next Area. Each Room you enter must be resolved before moving onto the next one. Rooms are resolved by rolling Character dice (white dice) to succeed skill checks or fight monsters. Your character gains more dice on leveling up. Exploration Resolve the Room card that your character is in. Once it is resolved, the two nearest rooms are revealed. Choose a room to enter. You cannot move up, diagonally, or left. Repeat until reaching the bottom right card. If you are on the last Area of a floor, you will then fight a boss monster. Otherwise, you move to the next Area. Each time you move to a new Area, you must consume one Food. If you do not have Food to consume, you lose 3 HP. How to Resolve a Room Each card has a type, name, how to resolve the room, possible roll results, and consequences -1 meat = Remove 1 Food Square-star = Perform a Skill Check Square-star ± 1 = Perform a Skill Check. If successful, you may add/subtract 1 to the Dungeon die result Black burst = Roll Dungeon die Black coin = If you pay 1 Gold piece, add 1 to the Dungeon die result Black coin ↔ Sack = Buy/Sell items Skull shield = Refresh Skills Hand and card = Item that may be picked up if conditions are met (e.g. paying Gold, Food, Skill Check, etc.) / = Choose one of the options ( ) = Optional. If resolving a Room requires a Skill Check, all Character dice (white) are rolled. If a 5 or a 6 is rolled, the skill check succeeds. The dungeon die (black) is rolled at the same time as the Character dice. The result indicates the outcome of the Skill Check, depending on success or failure. Combat Many rooms require you to fight an enemy. The player always attacks first, then the enemy. Combat continues until one opponent loses all HP. In co-op, players take turns fighting the enemy. Human Attacks Roll Dice: Roll all character dice, the dungeon die, and the Poison and/or Curse dice (if applicable). Poison/Curse: The Poison and/or Curse effects are carried out (if applicable). (See Status Effects ) Misses: Set aside any Character dice that resulted in an X (a miss). Critical Hits: You may reroll any dice that resulted in a Critical Hit (a 6). For each die rerolled, add its result to the total attack. But if the reroll is an X (a miss), no damage is dealt from that die. Feats: You may perform Feats (indicated by lightning bolt), which allow you to reroll a Character die result by paying 2 HP or 1 XP. You may only do this once per die. Potion: You may use one potion in your inventory. Apply damage to the Monster. If the Monster's HP have not gone to 0, the Monster attacks. Monster Attacks The Dungeon die's result indicates the Monster's attack--its success/failure and its strength. 1 = miss 2-5 = Successful attack. The monster inflicts damage as indicated on its card 6 = Successful attack. The monster inflicts damage as indicated on its card and is not reduced by Armor points. [Rating: 1/10] Neat for about a minute. Gets repetitive alarmingly quick. The locations aren't as varied as they initially seem, nor are the enemies. I could see this being improved with expansions adding new mechanics and a wider range of powers, card abilities, and monsters. As is, however, it's a slog of sameness bogged down by an annoyingly cyclic "Okay what do I do now? Roll the dice? Oh I didn't get a 5 or 6? Guess I'm screwed."

[Rating: 2/10] Just feels pointless and random. Roll 5-6 = win, roll 1-4 = lose. So many icons, so many rules, for such a shallow experience. It has all the thematic bloat of a dungeon-crawler, as if following a dungeon-crawler-cliché recipe, but without any intereting way of interacting with those elements aside from literally rolling a d6 and getting 5+. Couldn't even finish the game.

[Rating: 2/10] I think it's an overrated game. I like the basic idea, but in the end, it all boils down to rolling a 5 or 6 on a d6, or there's nothing you can do. There's no strategy, no decisions beyond deciding whether the next room is the one on the right or the one below, and then luck decides. It's not for me.

[Rating: 2/10] I really like the overall design and the quality is quite high. However the game is so random, most of the time you simply roll and prey. No decision, no random mitigation, no interest. Not a game for me.

[Rating: 2/10] Gameplay is close to non-existent. Most of the time it boils down to rolling dice and see what happens. Content is also close to non-existent. 20 room cards is ridiculously low. But to be fair there are only 8 room types and all cards from the same type feel exactly the same.  It's so boring that I didn't care to finish my first run (which didn't feel difficult at all but maybe I was just lucky as the game is pure randomness) and I'd rather do chores than play it again. [Rating: 3/10] Maybe I'm playing something wrong but after ten games I have the feeling the game is about 95% luck. The only moments where I do have a choice are: do I want to go to the right room or the room below next (sometimes I'm blind so that I can't see the rooms in advance => even more luck involved) and when to reroll (most of the time resulting in a loss of HP or XP => bad for the future). Everything else is pure luck. The original 9-card game did a better job because all the rooms were guaranteed, meaning it was kind of balanced. [Rating: 3/10] This game made clear to me what people mean when they say a game is 'fiddly' I sold this before I completed my first play

[Rating: 3/10] Way too luck dependent for what the game is trying to do. There feels like there isn't really a game arc here, nor are there many decisions to make. I know this game isn't designed for me and my first inkling here would be to just go play a dungeon crawling video game instead. That being said, even if I did enjoy this genre more, this feels like a very weak iteration of co-op dungeon crawling.

[Rating: 3/10] There is very little player agency and decision space in this game, to the point where it feels like a slot machine. It can be fun if you like gambling. Sometimes you win, which feels good, but it's mostly up to the dice.

[Rating: 3/10] Played on BGA.   Just to hard to do anything.  I mean if you like loosing in 3 - 4 moves, and just keep on trying for lucky rolls then it has some fun mechanic's on a dungeon crawl.   But otherwise I played like 6 games, 4 of them solo and 2 with a friend.  With the friend we got to at least 6-8 moves... but solo just died maybe I made it to the first big monster... 6 moves but just kept losing.

[Rating: 3/10] Played on BGA. Not a fan of this game. It feels like a crappier version of One Deck Dungeon. Too limiting and too punishing. Died early on the 2nd floor thanks to rolling misses and low hits on monsters encountered.

[Rating: 3/10] Played on BGA.  I played ten times, always in couple, sometimes with beginners like me, sometimes with expert. We never won. Also, experts explained that while in solo mode the game is almost easy, in two it becomes almost impossible.  So I can't play a game that is too easy or too difficult to win (and, for what they told me, it's not "my fault"). Should I think that this game has not been tested enough?
